description: Mobile-first adaptation of Epic detail Linked-issue rows and Dependency Graph degradation

tasks.title: LinkedIssueRow mobile-first scannable task line layout
tasks.description: Restructure LinkedIssueRow from a horizontal two-column card (flex items-center justify-between) into a mobile-first vertical task line: reading row (#number + title) on top, metadata row (health/status/priority badges, flex-wrap) below, then a start-blocker reason line, then a separate actions row. Change title from `truncate` to `break-words [overflow-wrap:anywhere]` so long titles wrap instead of overflowing. Add a pure-derived start-blocker reason function in `pages/epic-detail/model/` that returns a human-readable reason ('Another issue is in progress' / 'Waiting for #{n}' / 'Still a draft' / 'Blocked' / 'Not startable') based on LinkedIssue.startBlocker, hasInProgress, and health — rendered only when showStart is false (reusing canInlineStartRow as the sole gate). The Start button gating logic stays unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: LinkedIssueRow container uses vertical layout (flex-col), not the old horizontal justify-between two-column structure
Issue number and title are on the primary reading row; title uses [overflow-wrap:anywhere] or break-words, not truncate
Health/status/priority badges render in a flex-wrap metadata row below the title
Start-blocker reason text is rendered in the row when the issue is not inline-startable, with correct copy per blocker type (waiting-for/draft/blocked/in-progress/fallback)
Start button continues to render only when canInlineStartRow is true — no regression in gating
Pure-derived start-blocker reason function in model/ has unit tests covering all blocker branches
Component test asserts the vertical structure (class contracts), title wrap class, and blocker reason presence
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes with new and existing tests
tasks.output: Updated LinkedIssueRow in EpicDetailPage.tsx; new model/startBlockerReason.ts + test; updated/added component tests
tasks.notes: Design D1 (vertical layout), D2 (title wrapping), D3 (start-blocker reason derivation). Desktop also uses the vertical layout — no md: dual-branch. Keep Start button existing behavior and testid.

tasks.title: Remove action relocated to secondary affordance with confirmation dialog
tasks.description: Move the Remove button from the primary inline reading row into the separate actions row (established by T-001) as a visually de-emphasized secondary action (variant="ghost" or similar). Add a per-row local confirmation Dialog (removeConfirmOpen state) that opens on Remove tap — a single tap must NOT trigger removeEpicIssue.mutate. The dialog shows 'Remove #{number} from this Epic?' with explanation that unlink does not change issue workflow state, a Cancel button, and a Confirm button (variant="destructive") that is the only path to calling removeEpicIssue.mutate. The disabled prop (pending) from the page still controls the Confirm button. Update existing tests that click Remove and assert mutate directly to follow the new two-step flow.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove button is NOT on the same horizontal row as the issue number and title
A single click/tap on Remove does NOT call removeEpicIssue.mutate — the issue-epic link remains intact
Clicking Remove opens a confirmation Dialog with the issue number and an explanation message
Clicking Cancel or dismissing the dialog keeps the link intact and closes the dialog
Clicking Confirm (destructive) calls removeEpicIssue.mutate with the correct epicId and issueId
The Confirm button respects the disabled state when removeEpicIssue is pending
Existing tests that relied on direct Remove→mutate are updated to the two-step confirm flow
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes
tasks.output: Updated LinkedIssueRow with confirmation dialog in EpicDetailPage.tsx; updated component tests
tasks.notes: Design D4. Reuse existing Dialog component (same pattern as Close/Pause confirm dialogs at EpicDetailPage.tsx:905-985). Confirmation state is local to LinkedIssueRow, not hoisted to page. Do NOT use window.confirm (AGENTS.md: no real external systems).

tasks.title: Graph mobile degradation: horizontal scroll container and narrow-screen hint
tasks.description: Wrap the DependencyGraphWidget in the graph region of EpicDetailPage.tsx with an overflow-x-auto scroll container and give the inner canvas a min-w (e.g. min-w-[640px]) so it scrolls horizontally on narrow screens instead of pushing the page wider. Add a mobile-only (md:hidden, pure CSS) hint message above the canvas: 'Graph works best on wider screens — swipe to explore.' Ensure linkedIssuesView still defaults to 'list' and the List tab is always reachable. Verify tab toggle remains clickable at narrow widths (existing classes/data-testids unchanged).
acceptanceCriteria: The graph region contains an overflow-x-auto wrapper around the graph canvas
The inner canvas has a min-width that enables horizontal scrolling on narrow viewports
A narrow-screen hint message is present with md:hidden class (visible only on mobile, hidden on desktop)
List view remains the default (linkedIssuesView initial value 'list' unchanged)
List tab and Graph tab are both visible and clickable when graphAvailable is true
Switching tabs produces the corresponding view without error
Component tests assert the overflow-x-auto container and md:hidden hint exist in the graph region
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes
tasks.output: Updated graph region in EpicDetailPage.tsx; updated/added component tests
tasks.notes: Design D5. Pure CSS degradation — no useMediaQuery/useIsMobile JS hook. Use md:overflow-visible on the scroll container for desktop to avoid unnecessary scrollbars. Tab toggle (EpicDetailPage.tsx:798-828) classes and data-testids stay unchanged.

tasks.title: Graph unrenderable guidance banner, Error Boundary, and List fallback
tasks.description: When the graph is unrenderable, render an explanatory banner in the graph region based on graphRenderable.reason instead of leaving it blank: 'cyclic' → cycle explanation, 'empty' → not-enough-data explanation, other/fallback → 'Graph is unavailable'. Extend showList so it is true for ALL unrenderable states (graphSelected && !renderable), not just cyclic/empty, ensuring List is always the fallback. Wrap DependencyGraphWidget in a React Error Boundary that catches render exceptions and displays the fallback banner ('Graph is unavailable') while keeping List usable.
acceptanceCriteria: When graphRenderable.reason is 'cyclic', the graph region displays an explanation mentioning the dependency cycle
When graphRenderable.reason is 'empty', the graph region displays an explanation that there is nothing to render
For any other unrenderable state, the graph region displays a clear 'Graph is unavailable' explanation
List view renders and remains usable in every unrenderable scenario (showList covers all !renderable cases)
A React Error Boundary wraps DependencyGraphWidget and catches render exceptions, displaying the fallback banner without crashing the page
Existing cyclic fallback test (if present) is updated to also assert the banner message
Banner text directs the user to use the list below in all unrenderable cases
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes
tasks.output: Updated graph region with banner logic and showList extension in EpicDetailPage.tsx; new Error Boundary component; updated/added tests
tasks.notes: Design D6. Renderability type stays 'renderable'|'cyclic'|'empty' — unknown states are covered by the fallback banner text, not by extending the type. Error Boundary is lightweight and wraps only DependencyGraphWidget.
